prompt:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

The recommendation should be clear with clear follow up steps.

The recommendation is the call and the reasons for it, nothing else. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. State only the facts the decision actually turns on, and let the follow-ups carry what to do about them.

assessments.name: Identity
assessments.instructions:
Identity should answer: Is this a real business, and is it the one it claims to be?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity

assessments.name: Activity
assessments.instructions:
What does this business actually do, and is it allowed to do it?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.

assessments.name: Compliance
assessments.instructions:
Is this business, or anyone behind it, someone we're prohibited or restricted from doing business with?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits

assessments.name: Ownership
assessments.instructions:
Who actually controls and benefits from this business?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers

body.text: The entity exists and is the applicant. Name and office address both match a New York filing, the domestic registration is active, and 1 of 1 filings on the record is active. Entity type is a PLLC. The IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN and business name combination.

The submitted website and third-party profiles both check out: the crawl attributes the domain to the business with high confidence, and the profiles are online. No DBA filing is on the record, and no registration outside New York appears.

One thing does not line up. The filing names no natural person, the only officer carried is the entity itself, so JOSHUA GEE, submitted as the individual, is not matched to it. The website trades as Kairos Physio, a shortened form of the registered name that no DBA filing covers; New York does not require one for that.

Not a prohibited or high-risk industry. NAICS 621340 classifies it as Offices of Physical, Occupational and Speech Therapists, and Audiologists, under Health and Social Services, with MCC 8049. Both score 1 and neither is flagged high risk; the prohibited-list check returns Other Non-Prohibited. The merchant screen surfaced no risky keywords.

The entity form constrains the activity. A New York PLLC may only be formed to practise a licensed profession, so the business requires a licensed practitioner and its members must hold that licence. The website is online and attributed to the business, though it trades under a different name.

No licence check ran. The record carries no professional licence insight for the practice or for any individual, so the licence the entity form requires is neither confirmed nor linked to a person. The operating-as-claimed check and complaint themes were not ordered.

gaps.point: Whether a current New York physical therapy licence stands behind the practice, and which member holds it

body.text: No hits. Watchlist and sanctions screening returned nothing against the business, adverse media returned nothing, and PEP screening returned no hits on submitted individuals or their relatives and close associates.

The screen covered the entity and the one individual submitted with the application. Because the filing names no natural person and none was retrieved from it, no additional owner or officer was put through screening. People-level criminal history, litigation, liens and bankruptcies were not ordered.

gaps.point: Whether anyone holding or controlling the business beyond the submitted individual has been screened

body.text: No owner is established. The New York filing carries no natural person, the only officer listed is the entity itself, so JOSHUA GEE, submitted as the individual, is not matched to the registration. The website check did not match him either.

The record shows 2 connections and the connections check names them: KAIROS 801 LLC (confidence 0.96) and J.L.W. INVESTORS, LTD. (confidence 0.88). Neither is another business on this account. Both link by address only, not by any shared person: J.L.W. shares the practice address at 801 Madison Ave Fl 3, and KAIROS 801 LLC shares that address and also 21611 48th Ave Apt 3B in Bayside, which is on this business's own registration.

Membership is constrained but not evidenced. A PLLC is restricted by statute to licensed practitioners, so the set of people who may lawfully hold this entity is narrower than for an ordinary LLC, but no certification naming members, their percentages or their licences has been collected.
